title: All-Kinds-of-Fur (Allerleirauh)
summary: A king whose queen possessed golden hair was bound by a dying promise to marry only a maiden whose beauty matched hers. In his madness, he sought to marry his own gentle daughter....
full_text:
A king whose queen possessed golden hair was bound by a dying promise to marry only a maiden whose beauty matched hers. In his madness, he sought to marry his own gentle daughter.

To escape the unlawful union, the princess demanded three impossible gifts: a dress golden as the sun, a dress silver as the moon, and a dress glittering like the stars, along with a cloak made from patches of fur from every wild beast in the forest.

When the coats were delivered, the princess took three golden treasures—a ring, a tiny spinning wheel, and a reel—packed them inside a walnut shell, blackened her face with soot, wrapped herself in the fur cloak, and fled into the deep forest.

A neighboring king hunting with hounds discovered the creature in a hollow tree, named her Allerleirauh (All-Kinds-of-Fur), and put her to work in the palace kitchen sweeping ashes.

At three grand royal balls, she secretly washed the soot from her face, wore her sun, moon, and star dresses, and danced with the king, vanishing before midnight and leaving her golden treasures in the king's bread bowl.

On the third night, the king slipped a golden ring upon her finger. When she baked the bread in her fur cloak, the ring was found. The king seized her fur cloak, it slipped off, and her star-spangled dress and golden hair shone forth in royal beauty! The king embraced her, and their wedding was celebrated with great joy.
moral: True nobility cannot be obscured by rough fur; modesty and patient courage triumph over adversity.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
